Published online:
    August 26, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States (primary); Europe (ECB/euro zone), Canada, Japan, UK (secondary)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps July PCE, Q2 GDP, prior dollar moves
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — September Fed/ECB meeting pricing, Jackson Hole speech, month-end rebalancing
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    July PCE came in slightly above consensus (3.7% YoY, 0.2% MoM vs 0.1% est.), nudging Fed rate hike odds higher to ~40% for September. The dollar index rose 0.24% to 99.145. Fed Chair Warsh is expected to speak at Jackson Hole Friday but markets are skeptical he will offer policy direction. ECB's Schnabel signaled further rate hikes amid Middle East conflict and euro zone strength. Dollar sentiment remains mixed: Treasury Secretary Bessent's bond buyback announcement last week pressured the greenback, and Barclays flags a month-end dollar selling signal. CAD weakened on collapsed US-Canada trade talks; yen and sterling also softened.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — PCE inflation data, Fed rate hike probability, Fed Chair speech, GDP, consumer spending and CME FedWatch pricing are all central to the article.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 75 (moderately-high — rate hike is the directional lean of the data and Fed commentary)
Probability of increase: 40.1% (per CME FedWatch post-data release, up from ~36% prior)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 40 (present but secondary — market still assigns ~60% probability to no hike; Warsh not expected to guide)
Probability of holding: ~60% (implied residual from CME FedWatch hike odds)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (essentially absent — no meaningful cut narrative in the article)
Probability of decrease: ~0% (not discussed or priced)

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: +25 (mildly hawkish — PCE beat on both headline and MoM pushed hike odds higher, Boston Fed Collins explicitly flagged the need to hike soon, and ECB's Schnabel added to a global tightening tone; however, conviction is limited given Warsh's expected silence on guidance, the Bessent dollar-debasement concern, and Barclays' month-end sell signal keeping outright hawkish momentum in check)
